The other side of the sidewalk is semi-wooded with low growing evergreen shrubs. This sidewalk is about 100ft long, and has a trash can at either end. Also, in the last month, there have been a ton of flies buzzing around this area, so much so that the building manager called an exterminator. This morning, I (\~30s F) witnessed an intern (20s F) for one of the companies in our building walking into work eating a banana. About 3/4 of the way down the sidewalk, with a trashcan not even 25 feet away, she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. It landed on top of the bush and she just kept walking. I wasn't sufficiently caffeinated to be polite, so I blurted out "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" complete with the WTF hand gesture; pointing to the trash can. She ripped into me, claiming it's organic and feeds the animals. She was half yelling / half crying. I pointed at the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to "pick up your (her) damn banana peel." Instead she cried loudly saying something unintelligible, got her peel, and put it in the trash. I'm thinking, great, this is over. Maybe she won't toss her banana debris into the bushes and we will have less flies. I'm sure I could have been more nice about it / sworn less, but I was just so shocked to see someone litter like that. I badged in to the building and she walked in behind me. At some point, she must have cried to her boss about it, because her boss found me today and asked if I confronted her intern. I said I had, then explained, as I have done here, about the banana peel. I guess she spent all morning crying about how "mean" I was and couldn't do any work. My brain was screaming "drama queen" but I apologized instead for upsetting the intern. We laughed together about absurdity of it all, especially over a banana peel! But now that it's the weekend and I'm sufficiently caffeinated, I'm wondering AITA for calling her out?

Thanksgiving is next week and I'm responsible for preparing the turkey for the first time. My family has a specific recipe for it that everyone expects. How would you approach that?

### A Step‑by‑Step Guide to Your First Turkey Below is a practical, “first‑time‑maker” plan that covers everything from prep to plating. Feel free to tweak the timing or seasoning to match your family’s exact recipe. --- ## 1. Gather Your Ingredients & Equipment | **Category** | **Typical Items** | **Notes** | |--------------|-------------------|-----------| | **Turkey** | 1‑1.5 lb per person (e.g., 12‑14 lb for 8 people) | Fresh or thawed (24 h per 4 lb). | | **Brine** | 1 cup kosher salt, ½ cup brown sugar, 4 cups water, optional herbs (bay leaves, peppercorns) | 12‑24 h brine. | | **Seasoning** | Salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, thyme, rosemary, sage | Adjust to taste. | | **Butter** | ½ cup unsalted, melted | For basting. | | **Vegetables (optional)** | Carrots, onions, celery, lemon wedges | For stuffing the cavity or roasting alongside. | | **Equipment** | Roasting pan, rack, meat thermometer, aluminum foil, carving knife, carving fork | A good thermometer is essential. | --- ## 2. Prep Timeline (Assuming a 12‑lb Turkey) | **Time** | **Task** | |----------|----------| | **Day‑1 (Evening)** | **Brine**: Dissolve salt & sugar in water, add herbs, submerge turkey. Refrigerate. | | **Day‑2 (Morning)** | **Remove & Rinse**: Take turkey out, rinse, pat dry. | | **Day‑2 (Afternoon)** | **Season**: Rub with butter, then apply dry rub (salt, pepper, herbs). | | **Day‑2 (Evening)** | **Rest**: Let turkey sit at room temp for 30 min (helps even cooking). | | **Day‑3 (Morning)** | **Preheat Oven**: 325 °F (165 °C). | | **Day‑3 (Morning)** | **Roast**: Place turkey breast‑side up on rack. Roast 13 min per pound (≈ 2 ½ h). | | **Day‑3 (Mid‑Roast)** | **Baste**: Every 45 min, pour melted butter over the bird. | | **Day‑3 (End)** | **Check Temp**: Insert thermometer into thickest part of thigh (165 °F). | | **Day‑3 (After Roast)** | **Rest**: Tent with foil, let rest 20 min. | | **Day‑3 (Serving)** | **Carve**: Slice breast meat, then legs. Serve with gravy & sides. | --- ## 3. Detailed Steps ### 3.1 Brining (Optional but Recommended) 1. **Make the Brine** - 1 cup kosher salt + ½ cup brown sugar + 4 cups water + optional herbs. - Heat until dissolved, cool, then pour into a large container. 2. **Submerge the Turkey** - Ensure the bird is fully covered. - Refrigerate 12–24 h (longer for larger birds). 3. **After Brine** - Rinse under cold water, pat dry. - Dry skin is key for crispness. ### 3.2 Seasoning - **Butter Rub**: Spread melted butter all over the skin. - **Dry Rub**: Mix salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, thyme, rosemary, sage. - **Apply**: Sprinkle evenly, pressing into the skin. ### 3.3 Roasting - **Rack Placement**: Keeps the bird elevated, allowing heat circulation. - **Temperature**: 325 °F (165 °C) is standard; lower temps give more even cooking. - **Basting**: Butter or pan juices keep the skin moist. - **Internal Temperature**: 165 °F in the thigh; 165 °F in the breast is acceptable but can be slightly lower (160 °F) if you prefer juicier breast meat. ### 3.4 Resting - **Why Rest?** - Allows juices to redistribute, making the meat more tender. - 20 min is enough for a 12‑lb bird. - **Cover**: Lightly tent with foil to keep warm. ### 3.5 Carving 1. **Legs**: Separate thighs and drumsticks. 2. **Breast**: Slice from the center outward. 3. **Serve**: Arrange on a platter, garnish with fresh herbs or lemon wedges. --- ## 4. Safety & Tips | **Tip** | **Why It Matters** | |---------|--------------------| | **Use a Meat Thermometer** | Avoids under‑cooking and over‑cooking. | | **Keep the Turkey Dry** | Moisture on the skin prevents crispness. | | **Don’t Over‑Roast** | Dry breast meat is a common issue. | | **Let It Rest** | Juices redistribute, making the meat juicy. | | **Clean Up Early** | Prevents cross‑contamination. | | **Check the Brine** | Too salty can make the turkey taste overly briny. | --- ## 5. Optional Extras - **Stuffing**: Use a separate baking dish or a “stuffed” turkey (but be careful with timing). - **Gravy**: Use pan drippings, add flour or cornstarch to thicken. - **Side Dishes**: Mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce, green bean casserole, rolls. --- ## 6. Quick Checklist - [ ] Brine (if using) - [ ] Rinse & dry turkey - [ ] Butter & dry rub - [ ] Preheat oven to 325 °F - [ ] Roast (13 min/lb) - [ ] Baste every 45 min - [ ] Check internal temp (165 °F) - [ ] Rest 20 min - [ ] Carve & serve --- ### Final Thought Your family’s recipe is the heart of the meal, but the above framework will help you execute it confidently. If you have any specific ingredients or steps from your family’s recipe, feel free to share, and I can tailor the plan even more closely to your needs. Happy cooking, and enjoy a wonderful Thanksgiving!
